definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles mudaram de casa no ano passado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They changed houses last year.

thoughts: The word 'mudarei' is the future tense first person singular (I will change) of the verb 'mudar', which means 'to change'. This word will be primarily used to indicate a future action that the speaker will undertake. Given this context, learners should be provided with a straightforward definition of changing something.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mudarei de casa no próximo mês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will change houses next month.

thoughts: The word 'mudará' is the future tense, third person singular form of 'mudar,' which means 'to change' in Portuguese. A beginner learner would be interested in understanding this as a straightforward future statement about someone or something changing. This is a common and useful word for creating future predictions or plans that involve altering something.

definitions.note: Used for indicating a future action by a third person singular subject.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele mudará de casa no próximo mês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will change houses next month.

thoughts: The word "mude" is the first or third person singular present subjunctive form of the verb "mudar," which means "to change." In Portuguese, the subjunctive mood can express desire, doubt, uncertainty, or a hypothetical situation. Thus, its translation should reflect these uses, such as "(that) I change" or "(that) he/she/it changes." It's important to provide context in the example sentence showcasing its use in a subjunctive clause.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive mood expressing a wish, doubt, or uncertainty.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que ele mude de ideia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that he changes his mind.

thoughts: The word 'mudei' is the first person singular (I) past tense of the verb 'mudar,' which means 'to change.' In English, it translates to 'I changed.' This is a straightforward verb use where the subject is performing the action of changing something in the past. Beginner learners can understand this basic concept as part of learning common verbs and their past conjugations in Portuguese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem, eu mudei o arranjo dos móveis da sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday, I changed the arrangement of the living room furniture.

thoughts: The word "mudo" as an adjective typically means "mute" or "silent". In the context of describing a person, it refers to someone who is unable to speak or chooses not to speak in a particular setting. It can also describe something that is silent or noiseless. This is the most common use, so we'll focus on that definition for beginners.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou mudo de surpresa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was struck silent with surprise.

thoughts: The word 'mudou' is the third person singular past tense form of the verb 'mudar', which means "to change" in English. Thus, 'mudou' means "he/she/it changed" or "you (formal) changed". Beginner learners should understand this usage in past tense narratives or descriptions of changes. I'll provide a clear translation with a simple example sentence to illustrate this past action.

definitions.note: In the context of 'mudou', it is used for past actions indicating something or someone has changed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele mudou muito desde que começou o novo trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has changed a lot since he started the new job.

thoughts: The word 'muita' is a feminine singular form of the determiner 'muito', which means 'many', 'much', or 'a lot of'. It is used to quantify nouns and is a basic yet essential word in Portuguese, especially useful for beginners who are learning how to describe quantities. Given that it's a determiner, it appears before nouns and agrees with them in gender and number, hence 'muita' is used with feminine singular nouns.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem muita experiência no trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a lot of experience at work.

thoughts: The word is the feminine plural form of the determiner “muito,” meaning “many / a lot of.” Beginners should know it corresponds to plural feminine nouns. Provide a clear example.

definitions.native: many, a lot of, lots of
definitions.note: Feminine plural form of “muito,” used before feminine plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Muitas pessoas gostaram do concerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people liked the concert.

thoughts: As an adverb, "muito" most commonly translates to "very" (when intensifying adjectives/adverbs) or "a lot" (when modifying verbs). Those two English equivalents cover its core beginner-level uses. One clear example sentence will illustrate the adverbial function.

definitions.note: Used as an adverb to intensify an adjective/adverb ("very") or to show a high degree/frequency of an action ("a lot").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou muito cansado hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am very tired today.

thoughts: Provide only determiner meaning of "muito" (much/many) since pos provided is determiner. Include note about agreement forms. Example sentence uses masculine singular form "muito" before uncountable noun.

definitions.note: Changes to muita, muitos, muitas to agree with the noun’s gender and number.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tem muito trabalho hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a lot of work today.

thoughts: The word 'muito' as a pronoun is used to signify 'many' or 'much' as in a large quantity or number. It is used in sentences to describe or quantify a noun and is a basic vocabulary staple for beginners learning Portuguese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há muito que fazer antes da chegada dos convidados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is much to do before the guests arrive.

thoughts: "Muitos" is the masculine plural form of the determiner "muito" meaning "many / a lot of" when it comes before a noun. Beginner learners benefit from knowing that it agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies. Provide one clear definition with an example sentence.

definitions.note: masculine plural form; used before plural masculine nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho muitos amigos no Brasil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many friends in Brazil.

thoughts: The word 'muitos' as a pronoun is often used to refer to 'many people' or 'many things' in a non-specific manner. It is the masculine plural form, which could be relevant for learners to know when understanding agreement in Portuguese. I'll include a simple example that uses 'muitos' in a context that makes its meaning clear.

definitions.note: Used to refer to many people or things in a general sense (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Muitos vieram à festa ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many came to the party last night.

thoughts: "Muitíssimo" is an adverb derived from "muito," which means "very" or "much." It functions as an intensifier to imply a greater degree than "very," roughly translating to "extremely" or "very much" in English. In English, there is also the notion of "most," but the intense meaning is what is typically captured with "muitíssimo." Adverbs are used to modify adjectives or other adverbs, providing emphasis, so learners should see it in context to familiarize themselves with its usage.

definitions.note: Used for emphasis, to indicate a high degree more intense than "very."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou muitíssimo feliz com os resultados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am extremely happy with the results.

thoughts: The word "mulher" is a common noun in Portuguese meaning "woman". It's used to refer to adult female humans. This is the most direct and intuitive translation for English speakers, and the function is very clear in both languages. Because this is such an essential word in daily conversation, a beginner learner would benefit from seeing it in context. Examples should help illustrate its usage in typical sentences.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A mulher está falando ao telefone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The woman is talking on the phone.

thoughts: "Mulheres" is the plural form of "mulher," which means "woman" in Portuguese. Therefore, it refers to "women." Understanding the plural form is important for beginners as it helps in forming sentences correctly and recognizing when a text is talking about more than one woman. The example sentence provided demonstrates the use of this word in a natural context, which aids learners in understanding its application in everyday language.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As mulheres estão felizes hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The women are happy today.

thoughts: The word 'multado' is the past participle form of the verb 'multar', which means "to fine" in English. In this form, it refers to someone or something that has been fined. It's relevant for beginners to know it means someone received a penalty in terms of a monetary fine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi multado por estacionar em local proibido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was fined for parking in a restricted area.

thoughts: The word "multidão" is a Portuguese noun that translates to "crowd" in English. It describes a large group of people gathered together, usually in a public space. This concept is common in everyday situations, such as describing groups at events or protests. Providing an example sentence will help learners understand how to use the word in context.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A multidão se reuniu na praça para o concerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The crowd gathered in the square for the concert.

thoughts: The word 'mundial' is an adjective in Portuguese that translates to 'worldwide' or 'global' in English. It is used to describe something relating to or involving the entire world. An appropriate definition for learners would focus on this universal scope. I'll also include an example sentence for better understanding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A mudança climática é um problema mundial.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Climate change is a worldwide problem.

thoughts: Provide beginner-focused single definition for noun "mundo" meaning "world". Include clear example sentence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O mundo é grande e cheio de possibilidades.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The world is big and full of possibilities.

thoughts: The word 'mundos' is the plural form of 'mundo,' which means 'world' in English. Beginners will benefit from understanding its use in the context of discussing multiple worlds or realms, which is a common use case in both literal and metaphorical senses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Existem muitos mundos além do nosso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many worlds beyond ours.

thoughts: The word "muro" in Portuguese is a noun that translates to "wall" in English. It refers specifically to a wall or barrier typically outside, such as those that form the exterior boundary of a property or garden. This word is quite straightforward and is used often in contexts involving construction or architecture, as well as in everyday settings to describe barriers and divisions.

definitions.note: This typically refers to an outdoor or boundary wall.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O muro do jardim precisa ser pintado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The garden wall needs to be painted.

thoughts: The word 'muros' is in the plural form, meaning it refers to multiple walls. A wall is a common structure used for dividing or supporting spaces, which is an important concept for beginners to understand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os muros do castelo são muito antigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The walls of the castle are very old.

thoughts: The word "muscular" in Portuguese, just like in English, is an adjective used to describe something related to muscles or having well-developed muscles. In terms of usage, it can refer to anything from a person who has well-defined muscles to something that is part of or related to the muscular system. For beginners, focusing on its most common meaning - a characteristic of a person or an object (like an animal) with pronounced muscles - is important.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é muito muscular e forte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very muscular and strong.

thoughts: The word 'museu' refers to a physical place where artifacts, artworks, and cultural or historical objects are displayed for public viewing. It's a common and useful noun for beginners learning Portuguese, as it relates to experiences like visiting or learning about museums in cultural contexts. The primary English translation for this word is 'museum,' making it straightforward due to similar usages in both languages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós visitamos o museu ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We visited the museum yesterday.

thoughts: The word "museus" is the plural form of "museu," which means "museum" in English. This is a straightforward noun with no multiple meanings and is commonly used in both Portuguese and English. Beginners would benefit from learning how to identify and translate this basic vocabulary item, as well as understanding its use in context, such as discussing places to visit or cultural experiences. The example sentence provided demonstrates the word in a natural, everyday context, making it relatable and easier to understand for new learners.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os museus da cidade são muito interessantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museums in the city are very interesting.

thoughts: The word `musgo` in Portuguese refers to a small, soft, green plant that usually grows in damp, shady places. The most straightforward translation in English is "moss". It's commonly used to talk about nature, gardens, and forest environments. Beginners may encounter this word when discussing natural settings or learning about plants and ecology.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O musgo cobria as pedras no jardim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The moss covered the stones in the garden.

thoughts: The word 'musicais' is the plural form of the adjective 'musical' in Portuguese. It describes things that are related to music. This is commonly used to refer to musical events, instruments, or genres. The plural form suggests that it is describing multiple such items or categories.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os instrumentos musicais estão afinados para o concerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The musical instruments are tuned for the concert.

thoughts: The word 'musical' is an adjective in Portuguese and shares similar meaning to its English counterpart. It describes something related to music. This is an adjective, so I should focus the entry on how it's used to describe things associated with music in general terms, such as events, performances, or qualities. For a beginner learner, understanding that it's used to describe music-related attributes or contexts is important.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O festival foi muito musical este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The festival was very musical this year.

thoughts: The word 'mutuamente' is an adverb in Portuguese, which translates commonly to 'mutually' in English. It is used to describe an action or condition that applies equally and reciprocally to two or more parties. For example, 'They respect each other mutually.'

definitions.note: Used to indicate a reciprocal action or relationship between two or more parties.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles se respeitam mutuamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They respect each other mutually.

thoughts: The word 'muçulmana' is an adjective in Portuguese, specifically the feminine singular form of 'muçulmano'. It is used to describe someone or something that is Muslim or related to Islam. This is a commonly used term with a straightforward translation, and there's no additional note needed for beginner learners. However, an example sentence will help illustrate its use in context.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é uma muçulmana praticante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a practicing Muslim.

thoughts: The word 'muçulmano' is an adjective that means 'Muslim' in English. It is used to describe something or someone that is related to the Islamic faith. In Portuguese, adjectives must agree in gender and number with the noun they describe, but since 'muçulmano' in its base form is masculine singular, we'll focus on that form. In English, we use the word 'Muslim' similarly, both as a noun and an adjective. An example sentence is provided to illustrate its usage as an adjective.

definitions.note: Used to describe something or someone related to Islam.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele frequenta uma escola muçulmana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He attends a Muslim school.

thoughts: The word 'muçulmanos' is the plural form of 'muçulmano', which means 'Muslim' in Portuguese. It is used to refer to people who follow the religion of Islam. In English, the word 'Muslims' is used in the exact same context.

definitions.note: Refers to followers of the religion of Islam.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os muçulmanos celebram o Ramadã todos os anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Muslims celebrate Ramadan every year.

thoughts: The word 'má' is an adjective in its feminine singular form. It is derived from the masculine form 'mau,' which means 'bad' or 'evil.' This term is used to describe something or someone as being of poor quality or morally wrong. For beginner learners, it will be important to emphasize the gender and how it affects agreement with nouns. I'll focus the definition on its application as a common adjective for undesirable conditions or people. The example sentence will illustrate its use in context as a feminine singular adjective.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of 'mau'.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é uma pessoa má.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a bad person.

thoughts: The word 'mágica' as a noun in Portuguese generally refers to either 'magic' in the sense of the supernatural or to 'magic' as in a magic trick or illusion. For beginner Portuguese learners, understanding these definitions is key, as they encompass the common uses of the term in both everyday and specialized contexts such as films or shows. This is different from the adjective form 'mágico' which refers to something magical and would be used differently in sentences. The distinction and context in examples such as performances or storytelling would be relevant for learners.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele fez umas mágicas incríveis com cartas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He did some incredible magic tricks with cards.

definitions.note: Can refer to both the concept of magic and specific magic tricks in performances.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Crianças adoram shows de mágica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Children love magic shows.

thoughts: The word "mágico" is an adjective, which in Portuguese refers to something related to magic, enchanting, or possessing magical qualities. Beginners might come across this word in contexts involving fairy tales, magical creatures, or fantasy settings. The meaning is fairly straightforward and directly translates to English as "magical."

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O castelo parecia um lugar mágico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The castle seemed like a magical place.

thoughts: The word 'mágico' as a noun typically means 'magician' in Portuguese. This is the most common and straightforward definition for beginners. If it was used as an adjective, it could mean 'magical,' but the given morphology points to its usage as a noun. In this case, it refers to a person who performs magic or illusions. An example sentence will help illustrate its typical usage in context.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O mágico fez um truque impressionante na festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The magician performed an impressive trick at the party.

thoughts: The word 'máquina' is a noun in Portuguese that translates to 'machine' in English. It refers to a device or piece of equipment with moving parts that accomplishes some form of work. This is a common word and relevant for beginner learners to know as it is used in everyday contexts. There aren't many variant meanings that could confuse learners, making it straightforward to define.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A máquina está quebrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The machine is broken.

thoughts: The word 'máquinas' is the plural form of the noun 'máquina', which translates to 'machine' in English. For a beginner learner, it's important to understand both the singular and plural forms, although they mainly need to know that 'máquinas' is simply more than one machine. There isn't much contextual or secondary meaning, making it straightforward.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As fábricas modernas possuem muitas máquinas automáticas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Modern factories have many automatic machines.

thoughts: The word 'más' is an adverb which is a less common, more poetic or formal way of saying "mais," meaning "more" in English. It's not generally used in everyday modern Portuguese, so I'll clarify this in the note section.

definitions.note: This form is poetic/archaic. Normally, one would use 'mais' in contemporary Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele gosta de ti, mas quero te más.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He likes you, but I want you more.

thoughts: Given the morphological information, 'más' with a lemma 'mais' and part of speech as a determiner refers to the archaic or poetic form for 'mais,' meaning 'more' or 'most' often used for elevating literary language. However, for beginner learners, the most relevant usage of this word as a determiner is to indicate comparative or superlative quantities or characteristics.

definitions.note: 'Más' is an archaic or poetic form and not commonly used in contemporary spoken Portuguese. It might be seen in literary works.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele era o más valente de todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was the most courageous of all.

thoughts: The word 'más' is the irregular comparative form of the adjective 'mau,' meaning 'worse' in English. It's used to compare two things, usually implying a negative quality. This is a concept beginners need to grasp when learning comparatives in Portuguese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este livro é mais interessante, mas aquele é más.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is more interesting, but that one is worse.

thoughts: The word 'máscara' in Portuguese is commonly used to refer to a 'mask,' which can be the type you wear on your face for protection or disguise. Another common usage, less critical for beginners but still prevalent, is 'mascara' in the context of cosmetics. These meanings are quite different, so both should be included for the learners. For beginner learners, the focus should be on illustrating how 'máscara' can be used in sentences in these contexts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele usou uma máscara no carnaval.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wore a mask at the carnival.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela comprou uma nova máscara para os cílios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She bought a new mascara for her eyelashes.

thoughts: The word 'máscaras' is the plural form of 'máscara,' meaning it refers to masks or face masks. A beginner would be interested in this simple and common meaning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças estavam usando máscaras coloridas durante o desfile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children were wearing colorful masks during the parade.

thoughts: In Portuguese, the noun "máximo" can mean "maximum" in English. This refers to the greatest or highest amount, degree, or extent possible or attained. It is often used in contexts related to numbers, limits, or capacities.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O máximo que posso levantar é 50 quilos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The maximum I can lift is 50 kilograms.

thoughts: Single, clear meaning (“mother”). Provide beginner-friendly example.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Minha mãe gosta de flores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mother likes flowers.

thoughts: The word 'mães' is the plural form of the noun 'mãe', meaning 'mothers'. This word is quite straightforward for beginners as it's simply the plural of 'mother'. It reflects both the role and the familial relationship in both languages, thus is easy for beginners to grasp.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As mães adoram cuidar dos seus filhos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mothers love taking care of their children.

thoughts: "Mão" is a common Portuguese noun that refers to the part of the human body known as the "hand" in English. This word is singular and is used in many everyday contexts when talking about actions or descriptions involving hands. Given that it's a basic and frequently used word, it will be very relevant for beginner learners.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela usou a mão para abrir a porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She used her hand to open the door.

thoughts: The word "mãos" is the plural form of "mão," which means "hand" in Portuguese. It's important to show an example sentence that reflects the plural nature of this word. Beginner learners will benefit from a simple English translation of the Portuguese sentence that maintains the original meaning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela lava as mãos antes de comer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She washes her hands before eating.

thoughts: The word 'mãozinha' is a diminutive form of 'mão', meaning 'hand'. It's often used to express endearment or to refer to a small hand. Additionally, it can metaphorically mean help or assistance, often in phrases like 'dar uma mãozinha', translating to 'give a helping hand'. This usage would be relevant for beginner learners, as it's a common expression used for requesting help or assistance in a friendly manner.

definitions.note: Often implies a sense of smallness or endearment when referring to a hand.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem uma mãozinha delicada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a delicate little hand.

definitions.note: Used metaphorically in expressions like 'dar uma mãozinha' to mean offering assistance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou precisar de uma mãozinha para arrumar a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will need a helping hand to tidy up the house.

thoughts: The word 'média' in Portuguese refers to the concept of an average. It can be used in mathematical contexts as well as in general situations where one wants to describe something typical or standard. Beginners need to be able to recognize the term 'média' in everyday contexts where averages are discussed numerically or descriptively.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A média da turma foi 7,5.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The class average was 7.5.

thoughts: The word "média" is the feminine singular form of the adjective "médio," which generally means "middle" or "average." It's commonly used to describe something that is in the middle of a range, such as temperature, size, or some other quantity, which is crucial information for learners understanding contexts like weather or statistics. The feminine form is used when describing feminine singular nouns.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem uma altura média para a sua idade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has an average height for her age.

thoughts: The word "médica" is the feminine form of the adjective "médico," which means "related to medicine or medical." However, as an adjective, it refers specifically to something relating to a female doctor or medical professional in certain contexts in Portuguese. It is often used in the context of describing things associated with medical professionals or the field of medicine, especially concerning female practitioners.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the adjective, relates to medicine or female doctors.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela seguiu uma carreira médica depois de se formar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She pursued a medical career after graduating.

thoughts: The word 'médica' is a feminine noun meaning 'doctor' or 'physician' in English. It specifically refers to a female doctor. Including an example sentence will help illustrate its use in context.

definitions.note: Used specifically to refer to a female doctor in Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A médica examinou o paciente cuidadosamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor examined the patient carefully.

thoughts: The word 'médicas' is the plural feminine form of 'médico,' which means 'doctor' or 'physician.' Therefore, 'médicas' refers to female doctors. This form might be used to describe a group of women who are doctors

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As médicas trabalham no hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctors work at the hospital.

thoughts: The word 'médico' is an adjective in Portuguese. As an adjective, it relates to medical or health. Thus, it is used to describe things that pertain to medicine or the medical profession. It's important to provide an example that uses 'médico' in an adjectival context, so learners understand its usage beyond just the noun form which means 'doctor'.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela trabalha em um centro de pesquisa médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works in a medical research center.

thoughts: The word 'médico', in Portuguese, is a noun meaning 'doctor' in English. It refers to a person who is qualified to practice medicine. This is a straightforward translation and would be relevant for someone at a beginner level who might encounter this common profession in daily conversations, doctor visits, or when discussing health.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O médico fez um diagnóstico preciso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor made an accurate diagnosis.

thoughts: The word 'médicos' is the plural form of the noun 'médico' which means 'doctor' in English. It refers to medical professionals in the context of healthcare. Beginner learners would benefit from a basic definition and examples to illustrate its usage in common contexts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os médicos estão em uma reunião importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctors are in an important meeting.

thoughts: The word "médio" in Portuguese is an adjective meaning "medium" or "average", typically used to describe size, quantity, degree, or rank. It is commonly used in contexts like describing the size of clothing, the level of difficulty, or to express something that is neither high nor low. This aligns well with meanings that would generally be familiar or useful to a beginner learner, especially in everyday scenarios.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pediu uma camiseta de tamanho médio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He asked for a medium-sized shirt.

It's used in contexts where the objects referred to are feminine. Thus, the main task is explaining its use with feminine nouns or groups.

definitions.note: Used only with feminine plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Colocamos os livros na mesa, mas não há espaço nelas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We placed the books on the tables, but there is no space on them.

thoughts: The word 'nele' is a contraction of 'em ele', which translates to 'in him' or 'on him' in English. This word is specifically used to talk about a masculine subject or object, often referring to its location or position. Since it's a contraction, it might be confusing for beginners who are not familiar with the different forms that prepositions can take when combined with pronouns in Portuguese. Including an example sentence will help clarify its use.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela confia plenamente nele.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She trusts him completely.

thoughts: The word 'neles' is a contraction of the preposition "em" and the pronoun "eles." It means "in them" or "on them" and refers to a group of male people or mixed gender groups. It's often used to indicate location or place.

definitions.note: Refers to a group of males or a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Confio neles para terminar o projeto a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I trust them to finish the project on time.

thoughts: The word 'nem' in Portuguese is typically used as an adverb in the context of listing, negation, or adding emphasis there is a lack of one thing as well as another. A common usage for beginners would be similar to the English "nor" or "not even". It's often used in expressions or sentences where one wants to stress a negation or exclusion of things. An understanding of this usage as an adverb is crucial for forming correct sentences in Portuguese when discussing things that are not included or expected.

definitions.note: Used to add emphasis on negation or to say something is neither the first thing nor the second thing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele não gosta de futebol, nem de basquete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn't like football, nor basketball.

thoughts: The word "nem" is a coordinating conjunction in Portuguese. It is used similarly to the English word "nor" in negative sentences. It's often used to join two negative clauses. Let's create a simple example for learners.

definitions.note: Used in negative contexts to connect two clauses or words.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele não gosta de carne nem de peixe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He likes neither meat nor fish.

thoughts: The word `nenhum` is a determiner in Portuguese that is typically translated to "no" or "not any" in English. It's used to indicate the complete absence of something. For example, if you say "Não tenho nenhum dinheiro," it means "I have no money" or "I don't have any money." This determiner is important for learners to understand negation in Portuguese sentences, as it often accompanies a verb in negative forms.

definitions.note: Used to indicate the absence of something in negative contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não tenho nenhum carro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have any car.

thoughts: The word 'nenhum' is a Portuguese pronoun used to mean 'none' or 'any' in a context that negates the presence or existence of something. It is often used in negative sentences and can also translate to 'no' (as in 'no person', 'no thing').

definitions.note: Used in negative contexts to indicate the absence of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não há nenhum problema aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is no problem here.

thoughts:
'Nenhuma' is the feminine form of 'nenhum,' which is a determiner used to indicate 'none' or 'no' in the context of negation in Portuguese. It's typically used before a feminine singular noun. This word is crucial for expressing negation in a sentence, and understanding its use is essential for constructing basic negative statements in Portuguese.

In this context, beginner learners should note that it aligns with a singular feminine noun, and learning its usage can help them negate identities or quantities effectively in everyday conversations. The English equivalents "none" or "no" are directly relatable and simple for beginners to understand.

definitions.note: Used with feminine singular nouns to indicate negation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não tenho nenhuma dúvida sobre isso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have no doubt about that.

thoughts: The word "nenhuma" is a pronoun in Portuguese, functioning as the feminine form of "nenhum." It is often used in negative phrases to mean "none" or "not any." It is important for beginners to understand this word in the context of negation, as it helps to express the absence of something. Providing a note indicating its usage within negative contexts can aid learners in comprehension.

definitions.note: Used in negative sentences to indicate the absence of one or more items or people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela não tem nenhuma dúvida sobre o assunto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has no doubts about the subject.

thoughts: The word "nervos" is the plural form of the noun "nervo," meaning "nerves" in English. This word is used in contexts related to biology and psychology, often referring to the nerves in the human body or metaphorically to describe feelings of anxiety or tension. For beginners, it's important to understand both physical and metaphorical uses.

definitions.note: Refers to the biological nerves in the body; also used to describe a state of anxiety or stress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele disse que seus nervos estavam à flor da pele antes do exame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He said his nerves were on edge before the exam.

thoughts: The word 'nervosa' is the feminine form of the adjective 'nervoso.' It describes a state of being nervous or anxious, which is a feeling commonly encountered. This adjective can modify feminine nouns. Beginner learners will benefit from seeing how it is used in a sentence to describe a person.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está nervosa antes do exame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is nervous before the exam.

thoughts: The word 'nervosamente' is an adverb in Portuguese, derived from 'nervoso,' which means nervous. As an adverb, it describes the manner in which an action is performed, similar to 'nervously' in English. For beginner learners, it's important to show how adverbs modify verbs in sentences. The example should reflect this usage in a simple context they can relate to, such as someone giving a speech.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela falou nervosamente durante a apresentação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She spoke nervously during the presentation.

thoughts: The word 'nervoso' is an adjective in Portuguese, commonly translated to English as 'nervous'. It's a straightforward term that describes a state of being anxious or easily agitated. This word is frequently used to describe people or situations that are tense or stress-inducing. Beginner learners would likely encounter this in everyday conversation or basic texts, so it's useful to include a relatable example sentence that showcases this meaning effectively.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está muito nervoso antes da apresentação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very nervous before the presentation.

thoughts: The word 'nervosos' is the masculine plural form of the adjective 'nervoso', which usually translates to 'nervous' in English. Beginners would need examples that show the context in which this adjective is used, particularly in sentences describing people or situations that provoke anxiety or excitement. Since it's a plural form, the example should include a plural subject to illustrate its use correctly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os jogadores estavam nervosos antes do jogo começar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The players were nervous before the game started.

thoughts: "Nessa" is the contraction of "em" (in) + "essa" (that), used as a preposition followed by a feminine singular noun. A beginner learner needs to understand the meaning "in that" with an emphasis on proximity or situations already known or specified. An example could be how you might say "in that pizza place we went yesterday" but it informs the notion of specificity and "that" as closer in context relative to "aquela" which refers to something more distant.

definitions.note: Used before feminine singular nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Coloque o livro nessa mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the book on that table.

thoughts: The word 'nessas' is a contraction of 'em essas', which is a combination of the preposition 'em' (in, on, at) and the demonstrative pronoun 'essas' (those, referring to feminine plural nouns). This preposition is used in feminine plural contexts, where 'nessas' translates to 'in those' or 'on those'.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pensou muito nessas questões.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He thought a lot about those issues.

thoughts: The word `nesse` is a contraction of the preposition `em` (meaning "in/on/at") and the demonstrative pronoun `esse` (meaning "this" or "that"). It is used to indicate a specific location or time, making it more specific than just `em`, often translated as "in this," "in that," or "on this/that." This is useful for beginners to learn as it commonly appears in sentences requiring specification.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu encontrei o livro nesse armário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found the book in this cabinet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele escreveu nesse papel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wrote on this paper.

thoughts: The word 'nesses' is a Portuguese contraction that comes from 'em + esses,' meaning 'in these.' It's used to indicate something that is located within these particular things or contexts. The word is a masculine plural form, referring to specifically male gendered or mixed-gendered nouns that are plural.

definitions.note: Used for masculine plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nesses momentos, precisamos ser fortes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In these moments, we need to be strong.

thoughts: The word 'nesta' is a contraction in Portuguese formed by combining 'em' (in/on/at) with 'esta' (this, feminine singular). 'Nesta' generally means 'in this' or 'on this' when referring to a feminine noun. Understanding its use in context is helpful for beginner learners to become comfortable navigating contractions common in Portuguese.

definitions.note: Used with feminine singular nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O livro está nesta mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is on this table.

thoughts: The word 'nesta' is a contraction of 'em' + 'esta', where 'em' means 'in' and 'esta' is a feminine singular demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this'. Therefore, 'nesta' means 'in this' or 'on this', when referring to feminine singular nouns.

definitions.note: Used with feminine singular nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nesta cidade, há muitos parques.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this city, there are many parks.

thoughts: The word 'neste' is a contraction of 'em' and 'este,' used to mean 'in this' or 'on this' when referring to a singular masculine noun. It is an adposition (or preposition), and this contraction is quite common in everyday Portuguese. It's important to introduce this to beginner learners as they will encounter contractions frequently in Portuguese.

definitions.note: Used before a masculine singular noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tudo está neste lugar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything is in this place.

thoughts: The word 'neste' is a contraction of the preposition 'em' and the demonstrative adjective 'este'. It functions as a preposition in Portuguese, typically indicating position or time similar to 'in this' or 'at this' in English. Its usage is relatively straightforward, making it suitable for beginner learners.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu encontrei a chave neste quarto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found the key in this room.

thoughts: The word 'nestes' is a contraction commonly used in Portuguese, formed by the preposition "em" and the pronoun "estes," which means "in these." This word is used to indicate a location or a condition in relation to multiple masculine or mixed-gender things that are nearby in space or time. It's important for learners to understand the context of its usage, particularly with spatial or existential references.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nestes dias, temos vivido situações complicadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In these days, we have been experiencing complicated situations.

thoughts: The word "neta" is a noun in Portuguese meaning "granddaughter." This is a common and straightforward word used to refer to a female descendant of one's child. Beginner learners will benefit from understanding this simple family relationship term. I'll provide a basic example sentence to illustrate its usage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é a neta mais velha da família.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is the oldest granddaughter in the family.

thoughts: The word 'neto' in Portuguese is a noun which translates to 'grandson' in English. This is a straightforward family relationship term and directly corresponds to the English equivalent without any alternate meanings. The example sentence and translation given should make this family relation clear, and no additional notes on usage are needed as the context is quite universal and simple.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O neto visitou a avó no fim de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The grandson visited his grandmother over the weekend.

thoughts: The word 'netos' is the plural form of 'neto', which means 'grandchildren' in English. This plural form explicitly refers to more than one grandson, granddaughter, or a combination thereof.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meus netos visitam-me todos os domingos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandchildren visit me every Sunday.

thoughts: The word 'neutro' is an adjective in Portuguese. Its primary meaning is 'neutral' in English, which can describe something that is impartial, unbiassed, or without strong characteristics. For beginner learners, the main interest would be how and where to use this adjective in everyday sentences in Portuguese, corresponding closely to its use in English. Example sentences will help illustrate this usage clearly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cor cinza é considerada neutra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The color gray is considered neutral.

thoughts: The word 'neva' is a verb form of 'nevar', which means to snow. In this form, it is the third person singular present tense, meaning it refers to the action of snowing as performed by the weather or sky ('it snows'). This should be noted for beginner learners that in Portuguese, verbs often do not need explicit subjects when they refer to impersonal actions like weather events.

definitions.note: Used to describe snow falling; impersonal verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No inverno, geralmente neva bastante nas montanhas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the winter, it usually snows a lot in the mountains.

thoughts: The word "nevando" is the gerund form of the verb "nevar," which means "to snow." So, "nevando" means "snowing" in English. It's important for learners to see it used in context to understand how to describe weather conditions involving snow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está nevando muito hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is snowing a lot today.

thoughts: The word 'nevar' is a verb in Portuguese, meaning "to snow" in English. As a verb, it describes the action of snow falling, providing an image related to weather. This is quite straightforward and not likely to have alternative meanings for beginner learners, as it's a specific natural phenomenon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está começando a nevar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's starting to snow.

thoughts: The word "nevasca" is a noun in Portuguese and refers to a heavy snowfall or blizzard. This is a meteorological term that is useful for learners to understand weather conditions. The usage in sentences will typically involve describing weather events or conditions.

definitions.note: Used to describe a severe weather event involving heavy snow and typically strong winds.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante a nevasca, ficamos em casa para nos mantermos seguros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the blizzard, we stayed at home to keep safe.

thoughts: The word "neve" is the third-person singular present indicative form of the verb "nevar," which means "to snow" in English. Providing a simple definition and example helps beginners understand its usage in a sentence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Em algumas regiões, neve quase todos os dias durante o inverno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In some regions, it snows almost every day during the winter.

thoughts: "Neve" is a noun in Portuguese meaning "snow." It is a common word with no alternative meanings, so we provide a simple definition suitable for beginners. The example sentence provides context for how the word might appear in use.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A neve cobre as montanhas no inverno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The snow covers the mountains in winter.

thoughts: The word 'nevoeiro' is a noun that translates to 'fog' or 'mist' in English. Beginner learners should be aware that it's used to describe weather conditions often characterized by reduced visibility due to moisture in the air. The most relevant information for learners would involve understanding its usage in sentences to describe such conditions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O nevoeiro estava tão denso que não conseguimos ver o outro lado da rua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fog was so dense that we couldn't see the other side of the street.

thoughts: "Nevou" is the third person singular form of the verb "nevar" in the preterite tense. It means "it snowed" or "there was snow". This form highlights the use of "nevar" specifically to describe a past event where snow occurred. This is consistent with how weather events are often expressed in many languages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem, nevou muito na cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday, it snowed a lot in the city.

thoughts: Provide beginner-friendly entry for Portuguese pronoun “ninguém”, meaning “nobody, no one”. Include note about typical negative construction with “não”. Give example sentence where it functions as subject without extra “não”: “Ninguém sabe a resposta.”

definitions.note: Often appears with the negative word “não” earlier in the sentence (e.g. “Eu não vi ninguém” – “I didn’t see anyone”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ninguém sabe a resposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nobody knows the answer.

thoughts: The word 'ninho' is a noun in Portuguese and translates to 'nest' in English. It is used in the context of animals, typically birds, to refer to where they lay their eggs and raise their young. This is a concept likely to be familiar and relevant to beginners learning Portuguese, especially when discussing nature or animals.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O pássaro estava construindo um ninho na árvore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bird was building a nest in the tree.

thoughts: The word "ninhos" is the plural form of the noun "ninho," which translates to "nest" in English. In Portuguese, this would refer to more than one nest, whether they are literal nests built by birds, or metaphorically for places of comfort and safety. Beginner learners would benefit from understanding its basic translation and seeing it used in a common context.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os pássaros fizeram ninhos nas árvores do jardim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The birds made nests in the trees of the garden.

thoughts: The word 'nisso' is a contraction of 'em isso', which is used to refer to something previously mentioned or will be mentioned, roughly translated to 'in that', 'in this', or sometimes even 'on that' depending on context. It's a pronoun often used to draw attention to a previously mentioned idea or fact, making it relevant for beginners to understand how to use pronouns contextually in Portuguese.

definitions.note: Used to refer to something previously mentioned or a specific concept or idea.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não estou interessado nisso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am not interested in that.

thoughts: The given word 'nisto' is a contraction of 'em isto', which means 'in this' in English. It is used as a pronoun to refer to something that has been mentioned before or is immediately present. This usage is fairly straightforward and relevant for beginners to understand as it relates directly to referring to objects or concepts in conversation. The example sentence should clearly show how 'nisto' is used in context, providing an intuitive understanding of its use.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não vejo nada de errado nisto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't see anything wrong in this.

thoughts: The word "no" is a contraction of "em" + "o" (masculine singular definite article) that means "in the", "on the" or sometimes "at the" depending on context. Beginners should know it is used before masculine singular nouns. Provide clear example.

definitions.note: Contraction of the preposition "em" with the masculine singular definite article "o".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is in the car.

thoughts: The word "no" is a contraction in Portuguese that combines the preposition "em" (in/on) with the definite article "o" (the), forming "no." This translates to "in the" or "on the" when followed by masculine singular nouns. It is commonly used in everyday speech and writing.

definitions.note: Used with masculine singular nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está no carro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is in the car.

thoughts: "Nobre" is an adjective in Portuguese that can be translated to English as "noble." It is often used to describe someone of high social rank or possessing admirable qualities. This would be relevant to beginner learners, as many basic texts and dialogues might include descriptors of people and their qualities.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A família dela é muito nobre e respeitada na cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her family is very noble and respected in the city.

thoughts: The word “noite” is a common feminine noun that means the period after sunset. In Portuguese it covers both what English speakers call “evening” and “night,” which is useful for beginners to know. Provide one clear definition with that dual English translation, add a short usage note, and illustrate with a simple sentence where “noite” appears in singular form.

definitions.note: Refers to the time period from late evening through nighttime.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A noite estava fria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The night was cold.

thoughts: The word 'noites' is the plural form of the noun 'noite,' which means 'night' in English. So, 'noites' translates to 'nights.' This is a common noun that learners would find useful when talking about time, periods, or events that occur over multiple nights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passamos muitas noites olhando as estrelas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We spent many nights watching the stars.

thoughts: The word 'noiva' is a noun, and it specifically refers to a 'bride'. It is used to describe a woman who is engaged to be married or who is getting married. This is the most common usage and the one that beginner learners are likely to encounter, so it should be our focus here when creating our dictionary entry.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A noiva estava deslumbrante em seu vestido branco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bride was stunning in her white dress.

thoughts: The word "noivado" refers to the state of being engaged to be married. It is a noun and is used to describe the period between a marriage proposal and the wedding to follow. This concept is common in many cultures, including English-speaking ones, so it should be easily relatable for beginner learners of Portuguese.

definitions.note: Refers to the period when a couple is engaged to be married.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O noivado deles durou um ano antes do casamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their engagement lasted a year before the wedding.

thoughts: The word "noivo" as an adjective in Portuguese refers to someone who is engaged to be married. As an adjective, it aligns with this meaning, emphasizing the state of being engaged. This is useful for learners who may encounter descriptions of people in everyday language and need to understand statuses related to relationships.

definitions.note: Used to describe a person who is engaged to be married.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está muito feliz por estar noivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very happy to be engaged.

thoughts: 'Noivo' is a noun in Portuguese that refers specifically to a man who is engaged to be married.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O noivo estava nervoso antes do casamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fiancé was nervous before the wedding.

thoughts: The word 'nojento' is an adjective in Portuguese and corresponds mostly to the English adjective 'disgusting'. It's used to describe something that causes disgust or revulsion. definitions.note: This word is often used to describe something that is extremely unpleasant or repulsive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cheiro do lixo estava nojento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smell of the garbage was disgusting.

thoughts: The word "nojo" is a noun in Portuguese that translates to "disgust" or "revulsion" in English. It refers to a feeling of intense dislike or distaste. Beginners should be able to understand its straightforward meaning without requiring culturally specific context.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem nojo de comida estragada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is disgusted by spoiled food.

thoughts: The word "nome" is a very common masculine noun meaning "name." For beginners, this is the primary and overwhelmingly common meaning, so only one definition is needed. I’ll provide a simple, natural example sentence that uses the same singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual é o seu nome?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your name?

thoughts: The word provided is a past participle and adjective form of the verb 'nomear'. In English, this translates to "appointed" or "nominated". This is a common usage, for example, when someone is appointed to a position or nominated for an award. It will be useful for beginners to understand this word in contexts involving appointments or nominations.

definitions.note: Generally used for formal positions or nominations.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was appointed to the position of director.

thoughts: The word is a verb in Portuguese. Its basic meaning is related to the action of naming or appointing someone or something.
